subject: Finly discovery recap — next step: dedicated capacity sizing deep dive
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Elena Soto <elena.soto@finly.com>
Cc: priyom_das@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 28 May 2027 16:02:00 -0700
Subject: Finly discovery recap — next step: dedicated capacity sizing deep dive

Hi Elena / Tom —

Thanks again for a practical discovery call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum: 

- Recap: Finly wants to run generative summarization and named-entity extraction across incoming batch and realtime streams (peak traffic expectation: discussed ~600–900 QPS burst, baseline ~120 QPS). Goal is sub-200ms p95 on the realtime path and throughput-friendly batch processing overnight.
- Risk areas we flagged: model quantization effects on accuracy, cold-start latency for isolated pools, and observable cost per million tokens.

Next step (recommended): schedule a 60–75 minute dedicated capacity sizing + technical deep dive with our Serving & Ops engineers. In that call we will:
  * Validate traffic profile (payload sizes, concurrency, sequence lengths)
  * Map to GPU pool shapes and expected batch sizes
  * Run a lightweight runbook to confirm fallback/overprovision policy

Proposed slots (PT):
  1) Mon, 31 May 2027 — 10:00–11:15 PT
  2) Tue, 1 Jun 2027 — 09:30–10:45 PT

I've attached a short prep checklist and an initial mutual action plan so your engineering team can gather the sample payloads and auth/access details before the call. If neither slot works, reply with two preferred windows and we'll make it happen.

Attachments: finly-scaling-prep-checklist.pdf (application/pdf), finly-mutual-action-plan.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)

Quick ask: could you confirm expected 95th-percentile payload token length (or sample JSON payload) and whether you plan to keep inference in-region (US) only? Those two items will materially affect the pool sizing recommendation.

Thanks — I'll hold Monday at 10:00 PT tentatively until I hear back.

Best,
Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0142

From: Elena Soto <elena.soto@finly.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Berger <tom.berger@finly.com>, priyom_das@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 28 May 2027 16:35:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Finly discovery recap — next step: dedicated capacity sizing deep dive

Thanks Ben — appreciate the clear recap.

Both Tom and I are available for Mon 31 May 10:00 PT, please lock it. A couple quick clarifications before the deep dive:

- Token lengths: for realtime requests we'd expect ~60–120 tokens at 95p (summary + metadata). Batch jobs vary widely — some runs are 6k tokens average per doc.
- Compliance: we are covered under enterprise BAAs; we will need to confirm data-at-rest options and SOC2 evidence during the call.
- Do you need any sandbox credentials ahead of time for an initial throughput probe, or is sample payload + traffic profile enough?

I'll also upload a small sample payload set to the shared SFTP referenced in your mutual action plan.

Elena
VP Product, Finly
elena.soto@finly.com

Elena — great, locking Monday at 10:00 PT.

A few quick logistics items from the Serving side so we make the session productive:
- Please share a CSV or small NDJSON with 50 sample realtime payloads (anonymized) plus 10 representative batch documents. The sample helps us estimate sequence-length distribution to tune kv-cache/batching.
- If you have an API key or short-lived sandbox creds we can use during the call for a measured probe, send via the secure upload path in the mutual action plan; otherwise sample payloads are fine.
- Can you confirm expected concurrency for the realtime path during a sustained 5-minute window (example: 120 concurrent connections with average 5 req/sec each)?

Agenda for the 75-minute deep dive:
  1) Short intro + goals (5m)
  2) Traffic profile & sample review (15m)
  3) Throughput modelling & GPU pool mapping (25m)
  4) Latency SLO tradeoffs and fallback plan (15m)
  5) Action items + next steps (15m)

I'll bring the capacity playbook and an initial quantization recommendation based on the sample sizes you shared earlier. Looking forward to it.

— Priyom
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
priyom_das@redwood.com

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Elena Soto <elena.soto@finly.com>, priyom_das@redwood.com
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, Tom Berger <tom.berger@finly.com>
Date: Fri, 28 May 2027 18:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Finly discovery recap — next step: dedicated capacity sizing deep dive

Perfect — Monday 31 May 10:00–11:15 PT is confirmed and I sent a calendar invite to all.

A couple of practical items before the call:
- Upload the sample payloads to the SFTP path in the mutual action plan or share an expiring presigned link; mark the file as SAMPLE_PAYLOADS_v1.ndjson.
- We will run a short probe during the call to illustrate tail latency differences between an isolated dedicated pool vs shared hosted routing. That probe requires the sample payloads and an API key (we can use a short-lived token).
- We'll also bring a short SOC2 evidence checklist for your compliance questions; Tom, if you can confirm any additional compliance stakeholders that should join, flag them here.

Links: calendar (https://calendar.google.com/event?eid=finly-deepdive-20270531), booking (https://calendly.com/redwood/throughput-deep-dive?month=2027-05), hubspot (https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/1234567/deal/DEAL-8731)

Attachments included again: finly-scaling-prep-checklist.pdf, finly-mutual-action-plan.xlsx

See you Monday — we'll aim to come out of the deep dive with a recommended GPU pool shape and 30/60/90 day rollout plan.

Ben
